transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get this coordination meeting started. We've got tomorrow's inbound delivery -- one palletized lot of generator housings and one lot of communications cable reels -- and I need to publish final lane assignments before the receiving crew leaves today. The draft plan currently shows all three staging lanes as interchangeable with no special receiving controls listed. Before I assign lanes, I need to hear from each of you: warehouse ops NCO, movement control officer -- are there any changes or issues affecting tomorrow's receiving plan that I need to know about? Anything affecting lane availability, equipment, handling requirements, or sequencing?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Sir, I need to flag a critical issue. This morning I confirmed that only Lane 2 has a current floor-load certification for the 1,800-kilogram generator-housing pallet. The certification is filed in the warehouse binder, but it has not been added to the yard diagram yet. That's why the draft plan still shows all three lanes as interchangeable. The generator-housing pallet must go to Lane 2 -- Lanes 1 and 3 are not certified for that weight.

transcript.text: Sir, I have a critical lane constraint to report. This afternoon I received the carrier's vehicle diagram and confirmed that the cable-reel tilt-bed requires a 4.0-meter turning clearance that is only available at Lane 3. This diagram has not yet been included in the movement-control brief, which is why the draft plan doesn't reflect it. The communications cable reels must be staged at Lane 3 -- Lanes 1 and 2 cannot accommodate the tilt-bed's turning clearance.
